subject: Re: DPA & model-use terms — no-training commitment and subprocessor evidence

Subject: DPA scope question + no-training commitment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Medivance is very interested in Redwood for some of our internal automation pipelines. Before we move to procurement, we need clarity on a few DPA items from a legal/compliance perspective so we can budget and get internal sign-off: 

1) Can Redwood commit contractually that customer-provided data will not be used to train or improve models (no-training / no-learn)? If yes, are there carve-outs (telemetry, system metrics, aggregated telemetry) we should expect?

2) Please share your current subprocessor registry and whether subprocessors have access to raw prompts/responses.

3) Are there any cross-border export controls or EU->US transfer limitations we should be aware of for health-related PII?

We have an internal deadline of end-of-week for a vendor recommendation. Can you share DPA language or a redline we can circulate?

Appreciate it —
Alice
Alice Park
Sr. Procurement Manager, Medivance Solutions
procurement@medivance.com

Subject: Re: DPA scope question + no-training commitment

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Jonas (legal) and Laura (privacy) so we can get definitive answers and the evidence pack. Quick answers at a high level: 

- We can offer a contractual no-training commitment for customer data (customer content) as part of our DPA — this is a common enterprise add-on. There are typically limited operational telemetry carve-outs for platform health (e.g., anonymized metrics and system logs).

- We'll provide an up-to-date subprocessor registry and a SOC2 summary. Subprocessors do not get access to raw prompts/responses for customers that opt into a no-train commitment; instead they operate against pinned model instances or dedicated capacity depending on the deployment.

- For cross-border transfers we support EU Standard Contractual Clauses and can discuss EU-hosted dedicated/private deployments for residency if required.

Jonas/Laura — can you confirm the precise DPA language we can offer and attach the subprocessor file + SOC2 extract? Also, Alice asked whether subprocessors ever process prompt/response content under normal operations — we should be explicit.

I'll coordinate timing with procurement.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA scope question + no-training commitment

Alice — thanks, and good questions. Below is a concise legal summary we can include in the DPA/redline.

1) No-training / model improvement
We can include a clause that customer-provided content will not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any models maintained by Redwood or its affiliates ("No-Train Commitment"). Exceptions: (a) platform telemetry that is strictly limited to infrastructure/operational logs and is aggregated/anonymized; (b) regulatory/legal obligations; (c) metadata required for billing and routing. All exceptions will be described and limited in the DPA.

2) Subprocessors and access to content
Redwood maintains a registry of subprocessors. For customers who contract a No-Train Commitment, subprocessors will not be granted access to raw prompts and responses. Where we use third-party services (e.g., cloud infra, metrics providers), access is limited to encrypted artifacts necessary for operation. We'll provide the CSV registry and indicate which subprocessors are in-scope for the specific restriction.

3) Data transfers and residency
We support SCCs for EU transfers and also offer Dedicated/Private deployments to avoid cross-border transfers entirely. For health-related PII, we recommend Dedicated capacity or our Private VPC option.

4) Evidence and verification
We can provide: (1) current subprocessor registry (CSV), (2) SOC 2 Type II summary, (3) a short attestation letter describing our No-Train contract implementation and operational controls. Note that full SOC2 reports are available under NDA if Medivance requires them.

I am attaching a redline for the DPA that includes the No-Train Commitment wording and a proposed audit/evidence appendix. Please review and let us know any carve-outs Medivance needs.

— Jonas
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

If you can get the registry and attestation by EOD tomorrow it will help us move the vendor recommendation through our risk committee.

Regards,

Hi Alice — attaching the items you requested and a short operational note below. Links/attachments: subprocessor CSV, SOC2 summary, and the DPA redline (Jonas attached earlier).

Operational attestation (summary):
- No-Train Implementation: Customer content is routed to pinned model instances or Dedicated capacity where model weights and logging are configured to prevent incorporation into training pipelines.
- Access Controls: Access to customer content is role-based and logged. Subprocessors that require operational access (cloud infra, monitoring) are limited to encrypted logs or aggregated metrics; they do not have access to plaintext prompts/responses for customers with No-Train commitments.
- KV/Prefix Caching: We can disable prefix/KV caching for accounts that require additional guarantees; this is configurable per-customer.
- Verification: We provide an attestation letter describing these controls; full audits can be scheduled under NDA.

Attachment stubs included: subprocessor_registry_2027-07.csv, SOC2_TYPE2_2026_summary.pdf.

Let me know if you need a short recorded walkthrough for your security team.

Best,
